evals.name: verbose-research-report
evals.prompt: Run /help-me-understand:help-me-understand plugins/help-me-understand/skills/help-me-understand/evals/files/search-research-report.md. This is a test run: write the HTML page locally and do not publish it with the Artifact tool. Give me the path of the HTML file and the spec you rendered.
evals.expected_output: A research page that opens with a verdict picture of Typesense against Postgres full-text search, Meilisearch and Elasticsearch, each with the reason it lost, and a bottom line recommending Typesense; then short stops for when the verdict holds, a latency chart drawn from the measured p95 numbers, typo handling, a comparison table that highlights Typesense, and the unresolved warehouse-boost question as an open item; evidence detail in the Full detail drawer; the 2019 ranking-weight remark and the licence history in Also worth knowing; and one next action: run Typesense in shadow mode against the real query log for a week.
assertions: The page opens with a verdict gist that names Typesense as the winner and at least two of the other options with a reason each, and the bottom line under it recommends Typesense
page_type is research and the first stop states when the verdict holds (Elasticsearch past about 10 million products or heavy aggregations, Postgres only if typos are not worth the sync work)
A table compares Postgres full-text search, Meilisearch, Typesense and Elasticsearch, with the Typesense column highlighted
A bar_chart or dot_chart shows p95 latency with the values 180, 22, 18 and 35 ms; a bar chart starts at zero
The page states the monthly costs (zero extra, 60, 75 and 410 dollars) and the three days of index sync work that any dedicated engine needs
The page says when Elasticsearch would be the right choice (catalogue past about 10 million products or heavy aggregations) and when staying on Postgres would be
The unresolved nearest-warehouse boost rule (14 warehouses, precomputed field or re-ranking, not yet measured) appears on the page
The Meilisearch cloud-only features caveat and the Typesense GPL-3.0 note appear on the page, at least in the Full detail drawer
The 2019 ranking function that weights brand three times higher, and the Elasticsearch and OpenSearch licence history, are in Also worth knowing, not in the main sections
Exactly one Next action card, at the end, says to run Typesense in shadow mode against the real query log for a week before switching traffic

Under the bottom line the page says the reader may stop there and gives the stop count and reading time, contains no check-yourself prompts, has no leftover {{...}} placeholders, and contains no http or https URLs other than spec source links
Every section contains at least one visual block (any block except text, list, details, check and glossary), and the spec rendered without an "invalid spec" error

No section has more than 60 words of prose (text blocks plus visible list items), there are at most five sections, and supporting detail sits in the top-level reference list rather than in a final section of collapsed blocks
The chat reply contains only the file path (or link), the bottom line in one sentence and the next action, and does not paste the page

evals.name: dense-technical-answer
evals.prompt: Run /help-me-understand:help-me-understand plugins/help-me-understand/skills/help-me-understand/evals/files/postgres-bloat-answer.md. This is a test run: write the HTML page locally and do not publish it with the Artifact tool. Give me the path of the HTML file and the spec you rendered.
evals.expected_output: A concept page that opens with a chain picture from the five-hour reporting transaction to the growing table, with a bottom line naming both causes: the transaction stops VACUUM from removing dead tuples and the default autovacuum threshold waits for about 8 million. It explains MVCC with a concrete example before the general rule, shows the life of a dead tuple as a chain, stepper or flow, gives the threshold arithmetic as big figures, defines its terms once, has one or two check-yourself prompts, lists the four fixes in order, keeps wraparound and the evidence detail in the Full detail drawer, and gives one next action about the reporting transaction.
assertions: The page opens with a chain gist whose nodes lead from the long reporting transaction to the table growing, with the growth marked as the outcome, and the bottom line under it
page_type is concept and the bottom line names both causes: the long-running reporting transaction and the default autovacuum threshold
MVCC is explained with a concrete example (such as one UPDATE leaving an old row version behind) before the general rule
A chain, stepper or flow shows the life of a dead tuple: update or delete, old version kept, dead once no transaction can see it, space reused after VACUUM
The threshold arithmetic is on the page: 50 + 0.2 x 40 million, about 8 million dead tuples, about ten days at roughly 800,000 dead tuples a day
The evidence is on the page: about 11 million dead tuples in n_dead_tup and the autovacuum log line showing dead but not yet removable tuples
The difference between VACUUM, VACUUM FULL (ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock) and pg_repack is stated, for example in a table or before_after block
Transaction ID wraparound is explained, with age(datfrozenxid) about 310 million against autovacuum_freeze_max_age of 200 million

All four fixes appear in order: move or batch the reporting job (read replica with hot_standby_feedback off, or short batched transactions); per-table scale factor 0.01 and threshold 10000 (about 410,000 dead tuples); raise autovacuum_vacuum_cost_limit to about 1000; run pg_repack once to reclaim about 35 percent of 62 GB
Terms such as dead tuple, MVCC and the xmin horizon are each defined once (glossary strip or first use) and used consistently afterwards
The page has one or two check-yourself prompts placed after the idea they test
Monthly partitioning is in Also worth knowing, not in the main fixes
Exactly one Next action card, at the end, concerns stopping the reporting transaction from staying open for hours
